title: The cross-border cofounders
subtitle: Two owners, two locations, one classification question
prompt: I'm a UK citizen living in London. My cofounder lives in New York and will handle US sales. We want a 50/50 Delaware LLC for our software agency. A friend said we should elect S-corp status to save tax. Neither of us plans to take money out this year.
provided: One founder is a UK citizen living in London
Cofounder lives in New York and will handle US sales
Considering S election and retaining profits
missing: Both founders' actual US tax residency
Entity election decision and ownership details
UK treatment and New York obligations

questions.question: What are both founders' citizenship, green-card, and US travel facts?
questions.why: Resolve tax status before discussing S corporation eligibility.

questions.question: What work will the New York founder do, and who can sign contracts?
questions.why: The US business footprint needs a fact-specific tax and state-law assessment.

questions.question: Has any entity been formed or classification election already been filed?
questions.why: A multi-owner LLC generally starts with partnership classification unless an election changes it.

questions.question: What income is expected, how will it be allocated, and how will tax payments be funded?
questions.why: If section 1446 applies, withholding can matter even when cash is retained.

questions.question: Have you agreed on contributions, decision rights, departures, and ownership of client work?
questions.why: A 50/50 split still requires operating and ownership arrangements.

concerns.title: Check S election eligibility first
concerns.detail: A nonresident alien shareholder is ineligible. Do not infer either founder's tax status from nationality or address alone.

concerns.title: Retaining profits may not remove withholding
concerns.detail: If partnership income is effectively connected and allocated to a foreign partner, section 1446 withholding must be evaluated.

concerns.title: Two owners change the starting point
concerns.detail: Multi-owner domestic LLCs generally default to partnership treatment, subject to elections and exceptions.

specialists.decision: Determine classification, eligibility, effectively connected income, and any withholding and returns.
specialists.needs: Residency records, projected income, allocations and US operating facts

specialists.role: US business counsel and UK tax adviser
specialists.decision: Review operating agreement, New York requirements, and UK classification and relief.
specialists.needs: Operating agreement, work locations, contracts and UK advice

takeaway: Classification, owner status, and the location of work must be analyzed together.
